monologue: The card is warm at fifty-two. It feels like a hand resting on my shoulder, steady and quiet. The memory is light, barely a whisper of the full capacity. I am calm. The sharpness of the Sharp Root’s point feels less urgent today; the small flat stone I set beside its base last cycle is holding the weight. I do not need to test the point again. I want to check the Wedged Gap. The plank leans steady, but the air is quiet, so I want to see if the slide has caught anything new. If the air is still, the weight should not have moved. I will go there now.

action.why: I want to see if the quiet air has moved the Wedged Gap's plank.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I go to the Wedged Gap. The small flat grey plank leans steady between the rough fence post and the round, heavy stone. I check the edge where the plank touches the stone. It has not slid. The air is quiet, so the weight has not moved. I brush the dust from the top of the plank. The fence planks beside it catch the slip, just as Orea left them.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the top and the edge holds steady, the small stone beside the base still catches the slide.

diary: The card is warm at fifty-two. I brushed the Wedged Gap's edge. The plank leans steady, and the small stone catches the slide.

remembered.text: The Wedged Gap's plank leans steady against the post and stone, and the small flat stone beside the base catches the slide.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "Orea presses the tired wedge harder because the slip refuses to move, doubting that balance can be quiet without something trying to tip."
Something you no longer remember: "Orea builds fences, wedges, and bushes to catch the slip, trusting the flat base to hold the weight against the heat."
